utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Gustafson, I think I don't have to ask you whether you are ready to call your next witness because I assume that in front of us is Ms. Malm. Yes. Good afternoon, Ms. Malm. Before you give evidence in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite to you stand and to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Malm. Please be seated. English is not your -- the language you usual speak at home. If there's ever any problem, either in understanding or in expressing yourself in that language, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gustafson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Laila Malm.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter number 5365, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Malm, do you recognise this statement as one that you made on the 29th and 30th of July and on which you made some corrections on the 4th of September of 2008?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And is this statement true and correct to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Does it accurately reflect what you said at the time it was taken?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if I asked you in court today the same questions you were asked when you gave that statement, would you give the Court the same answers?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that statement into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the written submissions I see that there are no objections. Madam Registrar, that would be number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit number P774, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P774 is admitted into evidence. Which does not automatically mean that all the attachments are admitted. Ms. Gustafson, you may have noticed that there are out of, I think, 34 exhibits that the Gotovina Defence and I think it was the Markac Defence opposed against number 1, number 30, and number 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour and I spoke with the Defence briefly before the testimony and I have agreed that I won't tender numbers 30 and 31. I believe there's -- still an objection to number 1, which I intend to deal with during the witness's testimony perhaps objections could be dealt with then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then I think we could invite Madam Registrar to prepare a list assigning numbers to all the uncontested documents which we find in the -- in the 92 ter motion. Apart from admission into evidence also I understood that adding the documents to the 65 ter list would be -- that the attitude would be the same as to admission. Madam Registrar, do you have the list and the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In close cooperation with the case manager of the Prosecution, Madam Registrar will prepare a list assigning exhibit numbers to the uncontested exhibits. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, and I maybe correct this with -- I got the actual exhibit list that the Prosecution is going to involve itself with that was given to us, and my question is and this -- there's some source of confusion is -- are the exhibits because there is a significant overlap. Are the exhibits that are in the exhibit list as provided by the Prosecution the same as the exhibit list that are attached to the -- 92 ter statement that was given by the Prosecution. Because to that end, I believe in the 92 ter statement there was an exhibit of a homicide that was well -- was outside the area of the Split military district. So I'm a bit confused on which sheet counsel is moving from, the 65 ter list that was provided to us, or the list in the 92 ter statement and if there is an overlap or if they are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, Your Honour, they're the same. They're meant to be the same. Perhaps I could discuss this with colleague at the break. If there's a particular exhibit he is concerned about, I'm not entirely sure what the concern is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I can clarify it right now. And it is the issue coming up involving a report on 9/21/1995 in the hamlet Bolte/Kadzane [phoen] and it deals with a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I have two lists at this moment, the one is the one which is part of or attached to the 92 ter list that contains 31 documents; and then I have another one, apparently another list which gives more information and which is part of the hand-corrected statement of the witness. Could you -- if that's the one you're referring to, could you please give me the page number and the exhibit number, so that I'm -- I know what I'm talking about. Or what are you talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am talking about a document that is referred to which was initially part of the documentation supplied by counsel, if I may, that had the number on the top 00548120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That -- where does it appear on one of the lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the source of confusion, Your Honour. It came in with this bundle of documents from the particular witness, and I am having a difficult time, you know, assessing it, and I -- in the spirit of caution, I wanted to bring it to the attention of the Chamber because I am a bit confused about these multiple lists and whether or not this event is part of the submission of the Prosecution, in light of the fact that it's outside the scope of the -- it's outside the geographical area of the Split military direct and, frankly, it is it also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I have not been able until now to identify what document we are talking about, on whatever list. Guide me to a list and to a number or to a page and then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, as -- I'm sorry. As part of P774, there is a witness statement and if we go to page 17 of 21, in the middle of the page there is a reference to an UN CIVPOL report that is SO5-95/117.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... that you're referring to 177 instead of 117.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, 177, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, I have found it. Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that report does not form part of the 92 ter submission and I'm not tendering that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is mentioned by the witness but you're not going to rely on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I -- with all due respect, Judges, the bit of confusion is the list that is attendant to P744. There's a list that is attendant to the 92 ter submission and there's an exhibit list, and my confusion resulted from exactly what we were proceeding on, because, as you see, they don't necessarily coincide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I now do understand that this document -- that the Prosecution will not rely on that, therefore, it's -- it will not be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's a moot point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then to what extent the witness statement is still comprehensible without the document, we'll see that. Ms. Gustafson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this point I'd like to read a short summary of the witness's 92 ter statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you've explained to the witness the purpose of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Laila Malm was an UNCIVPOL monitor who was stationed in Knin between the 26th of August and the 2nd of September 1995, and then stationed in Sukosan between 2nd of September and December 1995. While she was station in Sukosan, Ms. Malm was primarily responsible for patrolling in the Gracac area. She went on daily CIVPOL patrols and received information about crimes such as murder, looting, burning, and mistreatment that were reported to her by people who remained in the villages in the Knin and Gracac areas. She personally witnessed a group of soldiers looting in Ivosevci village near Kistanje on the 30th of August, 1995. Ms. Malm and her colleagues recorded information they received about crimes in CIVPOL incident reports and reported these incidents to the Croatian civilian police. And that completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson. I take it that when closely cooperating with the registrar that you will also pay attention to those documents that are already admitted into evidence, such as on the list we find P251, P252, and P261, which are not necessarily all yet, but those are discovered already as being into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Malm, I'd like to ask you a little bit about your patrolling patterns. You have explained in your statement about your general pattern, how you went on patrols, daily patrols, generally with your colleague Mr. Martins. What was the purpose of your patrols, what were your tasks as CIVPOL monitors?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: The task was to monitor human rights violation.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So when you went to a village, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: We would leave the car, we would check the houses, if there was anybody there. If we found houses burned, then we would report it. If we found people, of course, we would ask them for the ID card, if they had ID card. Otherwise, we asked them to give name and date of birth. And if they had been violated in some way, we would made a report.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: What was the purpose of collecting the names and dates of birth of the people in the villages?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That was to keep track where does people live or not. And we also delivered food. We went very often to Knin to the Red Cross so then we went back to these people we met, to give them some food.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you've explained in your statement that you wrote your reports the same day that you received the report of the incident. Did you write those reports from memory or were you taking notes when you spoke with people?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: We were taking notes. Of course we had interpreter with us all the time, and we were taking notes and we usually came back quite late in the evenings, but then we went to the station and we wrote a report for each incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter number 5366.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This is a map that you used at the time and you've talked about it at paragraph 13 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the lower right-hand quarter of the document, of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you explained that you marked the villages that you visited on this map. The yellow and red or pink highlight marks on this map, are those your markings?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Are those the markings of the villages you visited?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And is there any difference between the red markings or the yellow markings, or no?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I believe that one colour is where we found people and another colour is where we didn't find them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Do you remember now which colour is which?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Not when I see it like this. If I can see the name of the village, I will probably remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the part where most of the markings are in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Are you able to see that, or would you like it blown up more?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I think it's okay. I think it is the red where we found the people. I remember Jarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And when you went to a village, did -- what did you do to determine whether it was empty or whether there was still people living there?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Well, if we found people, then of course we know that there were people.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if a village appeared empty, did you take steps to determine if there were actually people?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I believe -- I think that we marked it with yellow, we didn't find any people.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And what I'm asking is if you drove to a village and didn't see people in the streets, would you get out of the -- of your vehicle and look around or would you just move on?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: We even went into the houses, to check. Maybe not every house but a lot of houses and actually we found people. In one village we found a blind woman sitting on a -- on a bed, asking us not to kill her. That woman we -- we made a report and we gave it to the Red Cross, so they went to pick her up. Another man we found in the bed. He couldn't move from his bed also, so we went to the Red Cross in Zadar and after some discussion that man was also taken to, I believe, hospital, or I actually think he went to his brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Madam Registrar, that would be number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit number P775, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P775 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now -- if the witness could be shown 65 ter number 5368.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This document is one of the lists of people that you made, people in the Gracac area that you describe at paragraph 14 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And on the first page you see the letters WJ. Do you remember what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: This is -- I believe it's grids. Grid number.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And could we move to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You've just described how you went to the villages and recorded people's names and dates of birth. Are these -- is this created from your patrols and the information you recorded about who was left in the villages, their names and their dates of birth?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And how often did you update this list and the other similar lists?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: It was updated every evening. It was Luis who kept this list, so it was updated every evening by him.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So every day you would record the names of the people that you met that day?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown 65 ter number 5367.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Is this a similar list dealing with villages in the WK grid squares?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender these two lists into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One exhibit number or under two different numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: They can be under one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour. It's not really an objection, just a clarification. What is the date on these two documents? There is no date on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, could you clarify perhaps with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You heard the objection. Could you clarify what dates these lists refer to?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes. We started to make these lists, as far as I remember, almost immediately when we started on patrols and of course we were using these lists until the end of the mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You said almost immediately when you began your patrols. Is that when you began patrolling in the Gracac area?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, it is the end of August of 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness did not arrive any earlier, at least what's what I take from her statement. Madam Registrar, I do understand that it's is preferred by the Registry to have the documents separate under two numbers. Could you identify the documents and then assign a number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 5368 will become Exhibit number P776; and 65 ter 5367 will become Exhibit number P777.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P776 and P777 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if the witness could be shown 65 ter number 5374.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The document you're about to see is a memo that you and your colleague forwarded to the Office of the Prosecution in December of 1995, and it's described in your witness statement as well. Do you remember why you wrote this and sent it to the ICTY with your colleague?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes. We were very frustrated at this time because we felt that all these people didn't receive any help. They were intimidated. Their property was stolen. They were even murdered and nothing was happening so that's why we wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: By "all of these people" do you mean people in the Gracac area?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we move to page 2 of this document, please. If we could zoom in on the paragraph -- the last paragraph on this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And I'd like you to look at that last paragraph where it says: "CIVPOL has no cooperation from policija in Gracac. We have requested information from all cases in the weekly meetings for follow-ups but no answers." And a little further down it says: "In one case we have received information from policija that they have arrested one woman for theft of cattles. This information is not confirmed. In all other 56 cases concerning murder, rape, assault, theft, intimidation, robbery, looting, arson, and missing persons, CIVPOL received no information from Gracac policija." Now, this paragraph refers to requesting information from all cases. Was it your practice to report all the incidents you recorded to the Gracac policija?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Me and Luis Martins, we went there a few time to talk to them. Normally it was the team leader, Lennart Widen, who had meetings and brought it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And between your reports that you made with Luis Martins and team leader's reports, was it your understanding that the Gracac policija was aware of the incidents that you recorded in your reports?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this memo, Your Honour, and I believe that counsel may have an objection to part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, my objection when we came up with this was that I wasn't sure all this information was in the time-frame of the actual indictment or the charges, that is, from the end of September backward. And my question when we initially objected to this was: Were these issues that had taken place after the end of September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the Court's information, we also join in the objection for anything beyond the scope of the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could ask the witness about the time-period. I would point out that on page 4, 5, and 6, there are follow-up CIVPOL incident reports referring to earlier reports, many of which are in the indictment period, not all, but many them are. Some of them have exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, to that end, the ones that are discussing matters that are not within the indictment period I do believe it is incumbent upon the Prosecution to remove those from the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just as an example, the very first paragraph on the first page talks about incident in Vojnica and Glina and that has nothing to do with Sector South. So that is just an example.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the Chamber is able to determine which parts of this are relevant and which aren't, and my submission is that much of it is relevant to the time-period and the location of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, with all due respect, Judge, I don't believe that -- and while I have the highest respect for the Chamber's ability to cipher through stuff, when we ultimately come to the end of this I would suspect that the Chamber wants some guidance when they're looking at a document as to what is pertinent and what's not. And to that end, if matters here are outside the scope, then albeit not specifically date-identified but known to the Prosecution to be outside the scope of the indictment, it is incumbent upon the Prosecution to remove them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the other point along with that is that, you know, they have the burden of proof in this case and if they're going to start adding things that aren't part of the indictment and aren't part of Sector South and we have to weed those things out and point those things out, I think that's tremendously unfair to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would have no probative value for the charges would it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It would not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Now, the issue apparently is whether, as Ms. Gustafson tells us, that we should not redact the document and that it will be clear to the Chamber what is relevant and where there is probative value in this -- in these -- in this exhibit, and -- or whether it should be redacted so as to keep away from the Chamber those irrelevant portions. The Chamber will consider the matter and we'll take our time to carefully look at it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in your statement at paragraph 19, you describe reporting incidents to the Gracac policija. You say you mainly reported them to Ante Pogorolic, the chief of informations of the Gracac police, and sometimes also to the duty officer. When you reported these incidents to the Gracac police, did you go to the police station to report them?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like it ask you about the Gracac police station. Do you recall the building, recall going there?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing police in the area and patrol cars in the area?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: In the town of Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In the town or in the wider area.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I have seen it on check-points, I have seen it -- yes. On, on the fields also. I remember Mala Popina, I think I have other reports also where I have seen them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So in addition to Mr. Pogorolic and the duty officer at the police station you also saw other members of the police in the area?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 21 of your statement, you said: "Based on my observations, I don't think the Gracac policija put in sufficient effort to stop the criminals. We were able to visit all people in the villages and collect information on crimes but the crimes kept happening. I think the police could have done more to prevent crime from happening by, for example, stopping cars without licence plates and patrolling the villages more frequently." Based on what you observed in the area on your patrols and in your interactions with the police, who was patrolling the villages more frequently, you and Luis Martins or the Gracac police?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: We were there more frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And based on what you observed in the area, do you think the police could have patrolled as frequently as you were patrolling?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter number 4168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, the document on which the Chamber still will have to deliberate on admission has not been MFI'd yet. So that's the previous document. Madam Registrar, could you give us the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 5374 will become Exhibit P778, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It will keep that status for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If the text in the middle box of this statement could be blown up so the witness can read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, this is the incident of looting in Ivosevci that you described in your statement from the 30th of August. The report -- in the report you stated that many men dressed in military uniform were looting household goods from houses. And I'd just like you to describe to the Chamber more specifically what you saw the soldiers doing.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: What I can remember now is that we were travelling in our UN car. This village was on the right side of the road, and as I write in the report, we see all these people looting, carrying -- I don't remember exactly what it was now, if it was TVs or whatsoever, but they were carrying things into at least one truck. That's what I remember today.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And the report says: "We spoke to one them and they stated that they were protecting the civilians." Do you remember that comment?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember that, because what is what we usually did so I cannot exactly recall this incident but that's what we did. We asked people usually not what they were doing but if they saw people around or -- yeah. We were just a little bit of fishing what they were doing and to observe them so ... what I wrote here, that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Based on what you were seeing happening, did it appear to you that the soldiers were doing something to protect the civilians in that village?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the report it says: "Policija will be informed." Did you personally inform policija about this incident?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could that report be given a number, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P779.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P779 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to another report, which is 65 ter number 5377.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The report that is about to come up on your screen relates to the Gracac cemetery. It's a report from the 11th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if the text could be expanded for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I just add to the other report before that is -- the soldiers were screaming -- one of them were screaming that they would come after us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I think you mentioned that in your statement as well.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In your statement, when you describe this report about the Gracac cemetery, you said that the graves were visible from the main road and that's why you noticed them. Do you remember what it was about the graves or the graveyard that caused you to enter the graveyard?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I think it was the pile of sand and -- yeah, the crosses. That's what we saw from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you describe in the report and in your statement about a policija post there, and you stated in the report that it was 24-hour post. Do you remember now how you knew that it was a 24-hour post?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. Probably he told us this, this guy. But I don't remember. Because we usually left the area around 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And based on your knowledge of the area and your patrols and experience as a police officer, did you understand why the police were guarding or had a post at the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Did you see any other policija posts like this set up in the area, or was this the only one?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: This was the only one, except the check-points at the crossings.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Were there any permanent check-points at the crossings during the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember today if they were permanent.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could this report be given a number, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P780.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P780 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P261, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: The report that is about to come up on your screen is -- relates to an incident from the 13th of September in Brgud. And if we could move to page two of this document. In your statement at page 14, you explained that you remembered this incident and that you had given Prosecution colour photos of the bodies. I'd just like you to familiarize yourself with this report and then I'd like to show the witness 65 ter number 5372.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we bring up 65 ter 5372.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Are these the photos of that incident?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And the report that we just looked at states that you found the bodies outside house number 78.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we go back to the previous picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Do you remember where house number 78 is, in relation to this photo? Is it in the picture; is it to one side; it behind the person?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in your statement, you explained that you looked around after you found the bodies but you didn't see anything. Do you remember if you went into any of the surrounding houses?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to get a number for these photos, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objections, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P781.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P781 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like the witness to be shown 65 ter number 2041, and if it could be shown in such a way that is not visible to the public. And if we could move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you one or two questions about this report, and if could you answer without referring to the names of the victims that would be helpful. Do you remember this incident?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Right about the middle of this report it explains that the victim informed the police in Gracac. Do you remember if you spoke to the victim about any steps that the police had taken, or any investigation that it -- was taking place?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, I don't remember if we discussed that. I remember that we met a policija patrol there once, and we made more reports from these people there. They had visitors quite often, not -- not by the police, but by people who stole things from them, and I think she was beaten up also -- or other people. So we went to Mala Popina quite often.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And in general, if a -- if you recorded an incident and a victim or witness told that you they had reported that incident to the police, did you still follow up with the police about the incident or did -- or not?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: We followed it up, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like tender this report, Your Honour, and I'd like to tender it under seal to protect the privacy of the victims if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P782.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P782 is admitted into evidence. I have forgotten to add to that, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Malm.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, have I no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson. Who will be first to cross-examine Ms. Malm? Yes. Ms. Malm, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kehoe is counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could just have one moment, Your Honour, to get set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Malm.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm -- I'd like to ask you a few questions about what was just discussed on your direct examination and some of your reports, both your statement and your UN CIVPOL report. So if I jump around a little bit, bear with me, and if you don't understand any question that I ask you, please stop me.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Malm, first, when you were -- at the early part of August in your statement, you note that you were in Sector North, and I believe the town is Topusko, is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were there during Operation Storm. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The 4th and 5th? And if I can go to your 1997 statement, 1D49-0004. This is a copy of your 1997 statement. That's the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page, five paragraphs down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, before I ask you about this, Ms. Malm, the area that you were in was controlled by the ARSK on the 4th of -- up to the 4th and 5th of August of 1995, was it not?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you note in this report, in that paragraph, again, one, two, three, four, five, about halfway down, in talking about the ARSK: "Operation Storm started early in the morning of 04 August 1995. Topusko area was not shelled or bombarded. There was no military activity of the army of the RSK. Before Operation Storm, there was several battalions in the territory of Sector North but they did not resist Croats. They just withdrew from the territory the day after the operation had started. It seemed to me that they received such an order from the government, not to fight, to surrender weapons to UNPROFOR and flee to Bosnia." Just waiting for the translation to catch up with us. So the -- according to your statement, Ms. Malm, the ARSK withdrew and went to Bosnia almost without a fight on the 5th of August, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it seemed to you, did it not, that they received an order to do that or got some indication to do that.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That is it what we were told by the interpreters, the Serbian interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did those -- did those Serbian interpreters inform you that their ARSK communications with their headquarters in Knin had broken down?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No. I was told that the government in Knin had left earlier, before Operation Storm. That's what the -- the interpreters told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if I can just reformulate what you said. You were told that the government in Knin had left, so then all the soldiers left as well.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that when the people in charge of the RSK departed in Knin, the soldiers that were in Sector North chose to leave once they learned of that fact?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Most probably. And, of course, we saw RSK soldiers leaving with tanks. Because I think I was out on the street around 6th, 7th of August so they were still in the area going with the -- with the refugee convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So as late as the 6th or 7th of August, the ARSK military personnel, in conjunction with the convoys, were moving towards Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yeah. I remember I saw at least one tank with the -- with the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Malm, when you are talking about the events in Sector North and Sector South, you were aware that as of the 6th of August of 1995 that the constitutional authority of the Republic of Croatia took over all of the lands or the retaken lands in the Krajina. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You also mentioned your basic area of expertise was in the civil arena with the civilian police. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that accounts, I take it, for your statement in paragraph 23 of P774, that -- do you have that? I don't want to get too quickly ahead of you. Paragraph 23 of 774. "In general, I don't know anything about the relationship between the Croatian police and the military."

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am just trying to reference to you a point and then go to a next point. In your statement, P774, at paragraph 23 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could bring that up on the screen. That will be page 7 of that document. In the middle of that paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You see where it writes: "In general, I don't know ..." Do you see that Ms. Malm?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, in general, you don't know anything about the relationship between the Croatian police and the military because you were basically involved with the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when, for instance, P265 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could put that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I also want to make clear, this report is signed by me but Luis Martins was beside me when this Russian investigator from ICTY was interviewing me. So it is also his words in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, ma`am, just if I can correct it with the assistance of the Prosecution. The point that I just read to you on P744 is your statement of the 29th and the 30th of July of 2008. This is not the statement that counsel put in of December of 1995 where you signed it with Luis Martins. So just to be clear, and if there is ever any question in your mind which report we're talking about, just take your time and we can address them point by point, okay?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when we turn to this report, P265, and in this, which was mentioned in your evidence -- your 65 ter evidence, it notes that when you got to Otric junction, "we were stopped by a Croatian military and civilian police at their check-point." So this is a check-point manned by the MPs and the civilian police together.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you note: "They informed us that we were not allowed to proceed our patrol without special permission from Knin military authorities. They stated it is a military zone." Now, on the -- this statement which is the 20th of September, 1995, was the HV operating in that area on the 20th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember if I saw them that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, okay. So you don't know, as you sit here, one way or the other whether or not --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, of course, if they were at this check-point, of course, yes, since I wrote the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So other than the people at the check-point, do you know if there was military operations going on in that area?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Outside the check-point, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I would like to just touch on briefly some of the matters that you addressed concerning some of the issues that you discussed with residents of villages, if I may. And you talk about in some of your reports soldiers, individuals wearing military clothing, people telling you that people were walking around with military clothing on. Do you recall generally those conversations? We'll go into them a little more specifically. Do you remember those?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Well, I remember that quite often we were told when we made the report that it was soldiers in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at that time, did you know if those soldiers were demobilised troops?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: What is demobilised troops?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware -- let me back up. Were you aware that approximately the 9th of August, the HV demobilised 70.000 troops, approximately, and that is, took them out of service of the army of the Republic of Croatia. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that many people walking around in Sector South and Sector North wearing camouflage clothing were no longer part of the HV?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember if I saw people in -- civilians in camouflage. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if a civilian was in camouflage clothing, would you know that person was in fact a civilian and not a soldier?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, so there is some -- well, let us address a particular point and maybe we can develop this idea of who these folks are. And if I may go to your report that was just put in evidence by counsel on Ivosevci, 4168, and I believe that is P779.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could bring that up on the screen. If we can just blow that up just a little bit more. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, we -- this is a document that was just put in evidence. And it notes that you observed many men dressed in military uniforms. And that means camouflage, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And they were looting household goods from houses. They were travelling in one truck, plate number ZD 2353 AB and one red car, plate number ZD 34 U. Now, looking at that, Ms. Malm, you know that those licence plates are for vehicles that emanate from Zadar, don't they?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, likewise, you know that vehicles that belonged to the Republic of Croatia or the army of the Republic of Croatia begin with the letters HV, don't they?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So these individuals that were in this particular -- these two vehicles were in vehicles that were not part of the Republic of Croatia -- excuse me, the army of the Republic of Croatia, did they, or were they?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't know. I just report what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, ma`am. But you just told us that licence plates for military vehicles belonging to the army of the Republic of Croatia have HV in them and these have plates that are from the city of Zadar. And don't those plates normally or aren't those plates normally on civilian vehicles belonging to civilians and not the military?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn your attention to 65 ter 5380. I don't know if that has been, in fact, put into evidence yet or if we have a number for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't believe we have a number for that yet, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Shall I just deal with the 65 ter number and then clean it up later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the issue is that Madam Registrar prepared now a list for the exhibit numbers so we have to check whether the document you're referring to now appears on that list.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour. Then it will receive a number anyhow. Madam Registrar is kind enough to single it out from her list so that we immediately deal with this one. That would be, Madam Registrar ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit number P793, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to tender this soon, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this was part of the series of documents that were being presented by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was just dealing with it on cross because it was a part of that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then since there are no objections, this one certainly will be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have now on our screen P793. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Malm, just take a look at this report which is of the 20th of September. The gentleman that was in this informed you - and this is the third paragraph down - that: "On the 15th of September around 1530, three armed men between 35 years of age were in this hamlet and all of them used military uniforms. They parked two cars 200 metres from his house. One yellow colour, the other blue. Those cars with, I'm not sure, triller and without number plates." Now you use the term "used military uniforms." What you meant by that, ma'am, was -- or what this individual was telling you was that individuals were dressed in camouflage, but the implication is that they were not real soldiers. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: This report is written by Luis Martins, but -- yes, he probably means camouflage uniform. That's what I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But the further implication that in using military uniforms is that the people that came, these men that came were not active-duty real soldiers. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us probe yet further in this. We look down again and there are two vehicles, one yellow and the other blue, without number plates. Now, you know based on being in that area for sometime that those vehicles did not belong to the army of the Republic of Croatia as they had no plates with HV on them. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you got this information, ma`am, did you conclude, based on what this gentleman told you, that these three armed men who came to this village were not HV soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Well, I'm not even sure if the villager know if it was from the army or, as you say, if it is civilians then -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Likewise, if we could just touch on the end of this. I mean, you noted that you were doing quite a bit of -- you said -- during your direct examination you were doing more patrolling of villages than the civilian police. At least in this report the last sentence reflects that: "They also informed us that they -- now they started to see more often the policija from Gracac in the area on patrol." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So at least by this point, would you agree, Ms. Malm, that the Gracac police department was getting up to speed and was starting to get more active in patrolling?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Well, according to this Dragan Milanovic in Palanka village, it looks like, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now let us turn to 65 ter 5379, if I may. I don't know if we have a number for that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is another one that we don't have a number but it is part of the list of documents that was set forth by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Madam Registrar could help us out.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P792.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which, since you use it and since there are no objections, will be admitted into evidence as part of the list. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we look at this, this is a report that is the 9th of September -- excuse me, the 16th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If can you just take a quick look at that. Now, this reflects that on the 7th of August, I guess about the time that you still saw ARSK military personnel moving through Sector North, this reflects that a woman told you that: "In the afternoon of the 7th, 30 Croatian soldiers came to the village. They drank coffee with the inhabitants and then left." Did she tell that you these Croatian soldiers treated her well and just had coffee and moved on?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And she told you that two soldiers came back. Do you see that next sentence?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And took her TV set. Now, since the TV set wasn't taken when the 30 soldiers were there, when you were writing this report, Ms. Malm, did this information indicate to you that these two soldiers were operating on their own?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Well, they came back alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me take you -- let me take this. 30 soldiers are in there and they're drinking coffee, I take it, exchanging pleasantries with this woman on the 7th of August and they move on. They don't take any TV set, they don't do anything. Thereafter, two come back and take a TV set. Based on being a law enforcement officer, Ms. Malm, did that information indicate to you that these two soldiers were operating on their own and it wasn't some part of concerted military activity?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I think he is asking the witness to speculate. She wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're asking for conclusions. This witness has several times tried, Mr. Kehoe, to -- although in questions you were asking for conclusions to take you back to facts, which is right to do. Doesn't make much sense to ask these kind of conclusions. I mean, if any conclusions are to be drawn from that, why would we ask the witness whether the other 28 were looking in another 14 houses for televisions, what it would mean that they were coming back alone. The witness rightly said, What I saw is the two coming back alone. We do not know. You could ask the witness whether she knew where the other 28 were, whether they were still together, whether they were split up in groups of two, what they were doing, but it doesn't make much --it doesn't assist the Chamber very much if you, more or less, push the witness into the conclusions you consider the most probably ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, the witness can draw the conclusions that she has, but if I just may analogize those questions to the questions asked by Ms. Gustafson, for instance, did you believe based on operating in the area whether or not the Gracac police department could have patrolled these areas more than they had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have objected to that, apart from that it is part of the statement already to which did you not object, I would have listened to you, I would have dealt with it, and what is true for you, of course is similarly true for Ms. Gustafson without any doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will do -- Your Honour, I will be guided accordingly in the future and will be more vigilant in those objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ma`am, as you continue on this statement it notes that: "These two were dressed in military uniforms from the National Guard." When you were writing that, did you understand that the National Guard -- what did you understand the National Guard to mean? Was that the home guard units?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: National Guard, they are there to protect the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What element of the HV was the National Guard? Were they home guard units?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you wrote down here "National Guard," is that information that you received from this individual in the village?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you don't have any knowledge with regard to military formations above and beyond what these individuals are telling you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the information concerning National Guard, you don't have any information or knowledge about HV military formations and you're just writing down there what these individuals are telling you?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go to another point, which is 65 ter 5381.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I can just get the actual number, being -- it would be P794.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this report reflects in the bottom paragraph of this document as of the 22nd of September, 1995: "Many armed civilians are around to steal and intimidate who lives alone and without any chance to defend themselves." Do you see that, Ms. Malm?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, again, were you getting consistent information that there were armed civilians that were not in camouflage, that were not -- have any trappings of military wear that were committing crimes in the area?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember hearing that. This is Luis Martins who wrote this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it says that -- at the top of this page that you were present.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall being told this, that armed civilians are around?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No. I believe that he made a mistake in the writing there. Because I don't remember that I heard that the civilians were armed. The few people we met in Gracac I don't think they had any weapons at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ma`am, during the course of your witness statement, you verified that these were accurate reports. Are you now telling the Chamber that this report by Mr. Martins or whomever wrote this report was inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, but I cannot remember civilians are around. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So right now you're just saying that you don't remember this event? Or this comment.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Let me think about it for a few minutes. Can I read the whole report first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely, ma'am, absolutely. And let me say, Ms. Malm, at any time we're moving through these reports and you need more time to read one of the reports, please just advise me accordingly and we will take the time and I believe --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- the Trial Chamber would permit that.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yeah. No, I don't remember this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. As you sit here, do you have any reason to question the accuracy of this statement being given to at least one UN CIVPOL member --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, maybe I was too quick to answer then. Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You're going to have to just -- go into that a little bit more deeply. I was about to ask you: As you sit here, you don't have reason to question the accuracy of the statement be given to at least one CIVPOL member. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yeah. And it could be right, because I think I even myself remember to seeing one man in civilian clothes running from a house when I was about to enter the house, and he was carrying like a hunting rifle, so he ran away from me. And I think he was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let us move to 65 ter 924, which is P796. Now, this is an event of -- that was with you and Mr. Martins. And in this particular event, we have another particular crime and we have an individual that's in a white Volkswagen with no registration plate. Do you see that? It's in the --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yeah, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And after the soldiers left, the police did, in fact, respond to this village, didn't they? Look at the fourth paragraph down.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Okay, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, again with this white vehicle with no registration plate based on your knowledge as an investigator, that, likewise, is not a vehicle of the army of the Republic of Croatia, is it?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the last paragraph of this. It says: "Mr. Cvjetkovic informed us there is a lot of people dressed in military uniforms in the area." Now is that what he told you, ma'am, that people were dressed in military clothing, as opposed to describing them as soldiers and active duty soldiers that people were dressed in military uniforms? Is that what he said?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: That's probably what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move on to 65 ter -- and I want you to keep in mind the white Volkswagen that is in the document that we just addressed. And if I could move to 65 ter 5382, which is P797. This is again a report several days thereafter talking about a -- at least people coming with two civilian cars, one red and one white, without registration plates. Now, did you ever, when you were down there, make the connection between those two white cars that were operating in this same area in these civilian vehicles? Did you make that connection at all?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No, we didn't. And it looks simple when we see it like this, but with all these incidents that happens it was not that easy to connect different reports to each other. Because in the evening we could come back with five, maybe ten reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you came back with these reports, there was no attempt to synthesize the information so you would all try to understand exactly what was transpiring? For instance, whether or not these people that were operating in this white vehicle were civilians, operating without plates or if they were operating in a vehicle with army of Republic of Croatia plates? You never attempted to do that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No. We just collected the information and informed the policija and the Knin HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we talked a little bit about -- about Croatian soldiers. I mean, we talked previously about the Croatian soldiers drinking coffee with the woman in the village. There were other incidents when soldiers attempted to help individuals in the -- civilians in these villages, did they not?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I remember one couple. The soldiers came there to have barbecue once in a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did they assist the people in the village or did they --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't remember if they assisted them. I just remember that about the barbecue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, let us turn to 65 ter 5383 and that 5383 would be P795. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, P788. If I may, just correct that. 5378, which is 791.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: P791; I apologise. P791. If we could put that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm just going to show you a couple of reports, the first one being P791. This is an incident where an individual was -- they attempted to take his vehicle. Do you recall this, ma`am, and the soldiers tried to get it back. That's in the last paragraph, the second-to-last paragraph. And let me show you another document which is 65 ter 5383, which is P788.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The second paragraph refers to an intimidation here and the intimidation stopped because one of the soldiers told the other soldier to stop. Now, did those events -- I mean, those events transpire where there was intercession by one soldier -- by, I guess, another soldier who was trying to prevent these people being abused. Did that happen? Were you told about events like that during the course of your deployment?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Absolutely. I have it on report here, and it actually happened to me once also. I think you have the report also. A soldier who was trying to steal my glasses and one of the other soldiers told him to give it back, so, of course, it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if it's the time for the break or if you want me to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. I don't know how much time you would still need, Mr. Kehoe. If you have to look at your papers then certainly more than is still available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you, nevertheless, give us an indication after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll now have a break and will resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, could you give us the estimate I asked for before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At the most an hour, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Malm, just if we could just talk about the reports that you put into evidence generally. When you were seeing people looting after Operation Storm, be they Domobrani or people in camouflage or civilians, did you know that these people on many instances had their property looted between 1991 and 1995 when the Serbs expelled the Croats? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you knew at that point that many of these people were exacting revenge for what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I thought about it at that time. But as you ask me now, of course, I know that something had been going on before also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned in direct examination about the Gracac police department and, if I can just speak generically about it, that they didn't do much to stop crime and you didn't find answers on the progress of your investigations. I mean, first off, you didn't report everything that you observed to the Gracac police department, did you?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Not immediately. Sometimes it was the team leader, Lennart Widen, who brought it up with, I believe, the chief of policija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The fact is you didn't report every incident or possible crime that you observed, did you?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Not in person, no. But I reported it to the team leader, to the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let`s look at, on P774, paragraph 10. By the way, as we're bringing that up, just following up on the question that I asked you about people looting because they had been victims of looting between 1991 and 1995, did any of these people who were doing the looting tell you that they needed to take some of these items from some of these houses in order to live? Did any of them ever tell you that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No. I cannot remember that I even spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you didn't engage them in conversation as to why they're --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Not -- no, because they were quite aggressive, as far as I remember it. One person even threw a stone at us and, as I told you, I saw one guy running away with a rifle, so we did not try to stop them or speak to them about these crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, may I ask you one clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were talking about when you saw people looting and were you aware that these people were -- I take it that you're talking about categories rather than as person A, B, C, D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Categories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Otherwise we would have to establish the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, categories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- basis for this. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if I can round this out, you never went and talked to these people and say, Why are you taking products from an individual house and putting it in yours.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No. Not as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If can I go back to my question before about incidents, in paragraph 10 you talked about the incident where some individual threatened you, and in the last sentence of that paragraph, you said: "We did not report every incident such as this one."

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No. I don't think we reported incidents that happened to ourselves, actually. I think we -- we just reported when it happened to the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if a crime took place concerning an UN CIVPOL member that would not be reported to the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Not when it came to myself. I don't think I did it, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But that was your decision, that wasn't UN policy, I trust?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think I was at that time more concerned about the civilians in the area than myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, ma`am, your reports to the Gracac police department, they were oral reports. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I believe so. I remember one incident we went to the duty officer, so that's oral.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Paragraph 19 of the same document that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Pardon? Paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 19. You'll see it.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Uh-huh, uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, four lines down in paragraph 19: "Our reports were verbal." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Paragraph 19.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: 19, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Four lines down.

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Uh-huh, yes. Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In your home jurisdiction in Sweden, are your police reports when you convey information to another police department, is that verbal or in writing?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I suppose it depends what it is concerning. But in this case if we went there, we didn't even have the report ready. So we had to go and inform them this is what happened maybe two hours ago. This is the information we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Malm, in your home jurisdiction if you routinely provide -- if you provide information from one police department to another, do you routinely do that verbally or in writing?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Well, I don't do it myself; it is higher chiefs. If I receive a report from a -- or an incident from a civilian, of course, I will write it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ma`am, let me continue on here. You said that they didn't do enough to stop crime. When it came to getting around check-points, you could easily get around check-points, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: Easily, I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get around check-points --

utterances.speaker: LAILA MALM
utterances.text: I remember once that we were being stopped. That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you get around a check-point?
